statement: Let F be any CNF on Boolean variables x_1,...,x_n with clauses C_1,...,C_m; clauses may be empty, tautological, or contain repeated literals. For each j let A_j be the set of assignments falsifying C_j. For S subseteq [m], let V(S) be the variables occurring in the selected clauses, and call S consistent when the simultaneous requirements falsifying every selected clause assign each variable at most one Boolean value. Then |intersection_{j in S} A_j| equals 2^(n-|V(S)|) if S is consistent and 0 otherwise (with the empty intersection for S=empty equal to 2^n). Consequently #SAT(F)=sum_{S subseteq[m]} (-1)^|S| |intersection_{j in S} A_j|.
proof: For each clause C_j, an assignment falsifies it exactly when every literal occurrence is false. A positive occurrence x_i requires x_i=0, and a negative occurrence ¬x_i requires x_i=1. Repeated occurrences repeat a requirement without changing it. If a clause is tautological, it contains both signs of some variable, so its falsification requirements conflict and A_j is empty. For selected clauses S, their intersection is the set of assignments satisfying the union of their falsification requirements. If any variable is required to take both values, this set is empty. Otherwise every variable in V(S) is fixed to one value and each of the other n-|V(S)| variables is free, giving 2^(n-|V(S)|) assignments. For S empty there are no requirements, so the intersection has size 2^n. An assignment satisfies F exactly when it lies outside the union of the A_j. Finite inclusion-exclusion for this union gives the stated sum.

statement: Lemma (restricted formula-to-roABP conversion). Let F be an arithmetic formula over a field with s nodes, in which each variable occurs at most once. There is a layered read-once oblivious arithmetic branching program computing exactly F, with a single variable order and size O(s^2). If F is linear in a designated set of placeholder variables, the computed polynomial remains linear in those placeholders.
proof: Induct on the formula tree. At each node choose a variable order by concatenating the orders of its two children; variables in the children are disjoint because each variable occurs at most once. For a product node, concatenate the child programs in that order, identifying the first program's sink with the second program's source; this computes the product. For a sum node, put the two child programs in parallel between a common source and sink; this computes the sum. Pad each branch at variables absent from that branch with constant-1 edges, so both branches use the same full order. Constants and variable leaves have constant-size programs. At any node the program has O(s) vertices and edges, and at most s variable layers; padding therefore uses O(s^2) edges overall. The construction preserves the computed polynomial at every node, hence preserves linearity in the designated placeholders when F has that property. The construction is uniform from the formula tree.
scope: This applies only to formulas with each variable occurring at most once. It does not show that a general IPS refutation has such a formula, nor that the resulting program satisfies any additional IPS axiom-placeholder conditions.

statement: Exponential-size representation lemma. Let F be an arithmetic formula over a field with s nodes, and suppose each variable occurs at most once in F. Then F has a uniform layered read-once oblivious arithmetic branching program, with one fixed order of the variables of F, of size O(s 2^s), computing exactly the same polynomial. Consequently, if F computes a polynomial linear in designated placeholder variables, the ABP computes a polynomial linear in those placeholders.
proof: Expand F by distributivity, retaining monomial occurrences rather than combining equal monomials. The number T(F) of occurrences is at most 2^s: for a leaf T=1; at a sum node T(F1+F2)=T(F1)+T(F2), and at a product node T(F1F2)=T(F1)T(F2). Induction on the formula tree gives T(F)≤2^s. Because F is syntactically read-once, each monomial occurrence contains each variable at most once. Fix any order of the at most s variables appearing in F. For each monomial occurrence, make one source-to-sink path with one layer per variable: at a variable present in the monomial use an edge labeled by that variable, and otherwise use an edge labeled 1; place the monomial coefficient on one edge (or on a separate initial edge). Put these paths in parallel by identifying their sources and sinks. Every path computes its monomial, so path-sum semantics computes exactly the expanded polynomial, hence F. The program is layered in the fixed variable order and reads each variable at most once on every path. Each path uses O(s) edges and there are at most 2^s paths, giving O(s2^s) size. The construction is uniform from the formula tree. Since the computed polynomial is unchanged, any polynomial identity it satisfies, including linearity in designated placeholders, is preserved.

statement: Let F be a CNF over variables partitioned into X and Y, with t clauses containing variables from both parts. Define M_F[a,b]=1 iff the assignment (a,b) satisfies F. Over Q, rank(M_F) <= 2^t.
proof: For each clause C, let h_C(a,b) be 1 iff C is falsified. If C uses only X or only Y, its satisfaction indicator 1-h_C depends only on that side. For each crossing clause C, its falsification indicator factors as h_C(a,b)=u_C(a)v_C(b): u_C records that all literals of C on X are false, and v_C records that all literals on Y are false. Thus M_F[a,b] is the product of the internal-clause satisfaction factors and the crossing factors (1-u_C(a)v_C(b)). Expanding the latter product gives a sum over subsets S of the t crossing clauses. Each summand is (-1)^|S| times a product of functions of a and a product of functions of b, hence is a rank-at-most-one matrix. There are 2^t summands, so rank(M_F) <= 2^t.

Proof: Write F = sum_alpha c_alpha x_1^alpha_1 ... x_k^alpha_k over exponent vectors alpha with sum alpha_i <= d. There are at most binom(d+k,k) such vectors. For each nonzero monomial, create a source-to-sink path whose edge labels, in the fixed variable order, are alpha_i copies of x_i for each i, with the coefficient c_alpha on one edge; the path weight is that monomial. Put these paths in parallel by merging their sources and sinks, so the path-sum is F. Each path has at most d variable edges plus at most one coefficient edge, hence the size is O(d * binom(d+k,k)) (with the constant and zero-polynomial cases represented directly). The construction is effective from the coefficient list. This proves an ordinary layered oblivious ABP representation for bounded-variable-support polynomials; it does not imply a read-once ABP representation when some exponent alpha_i exceeds one.
